title: How to spot good quality imitation jewellery before you buy
description: A practical checklist to judge imitation jewellery in a shop or online: plating, stone settings, weight, hooks, back finish and the red flags to avoid.
keywords: how to check quality of imitation jewellery
how to identify good fashion jewellery
intro: Good imitation jewellery is easy to recognise once you know where to look: even plating, front and back; stones that sit flat and firm; strong hooks and joints; and a finish that looks the same in daylight as in the photo. Price alone is not a reliable guide, so it pays to spend two minutes checking a piece before you buy it, whether you are standing at a counter or scrolling on your phone.

sections.heading: Start with the back, not the front
paragraphs: Every seller makes the front look good. The back tells you how much care went into the piece. Turn a necklace or pair of earrings over and look for a smooth, even finish. Rough metal, uneven plating, glue blobs or bare patches on the reverse side usually mean corners were cut elsewhere too.

In Kundan pieces, a neatly finished back, whether plain plated or decorated with meena colour, is a good sign. In AD pieces, look at the underside of the stones: open settings that let light through usually sparkle more than solid, closed ones.

sections.heading: The two-minute in-hand checklist
paragraphs: If you can hold the piece, run through these quickly:
list: Plating: tilt it under light. The colour should be even, with no darker or brassy spots on edges and corners.
Stones: press gently with a fingertip. Nothing should move, click or wobble.
Rows and patterns: stones in a line should be the same size and shade, evenly spaced.
Edges: run a finger along the inside of a necklace. Sharp edges will scratch skin and catch on fabric.
Joints and links: the necklace should drape smoothly and lie flat, not twist or stand stiff.
Hooks and clasps: open and close them. They should snap shut and not bend easily.
Pearls and drops: tug lightly. Loops should be closed, not just bent wire.

sections.heading: Weight: what it does and does not tell you
paragraphs: Many people judge fashion jewellery by weight, but heavy does not always mean better. A brass-based Kundan necklace will naturally feel more solid than a light alloy one, and that solidity often goes with better detailing and plating. On the other hand, very heavy earrings can be uncomfortable for a whole evening.

What you really want is balance: a necklace that sits centred without the pendant flipping, and earrings that hang straight without pulling the lobe forward. If you plan to wear a piece for hours at a wedding, comfort matters as much as looks.

sections.heading: How to judge quality when buying online
paragraphs: Online shopping removes the touch test, so you have to read more carefully. A trustworthy listing usually tells you the base metal, the type of plating, the stone type and the size or length. Vague listings that only say 'premium quality' are not giving you much.

Zoom in on every photo. Look for close-ups of the stones and the back, and for at least one picture in natural light. Customer photos and reviews are often more honest than studio images, and a product video shows how the stones catch light.

Finally, check the store policies before you order. Varaha, for example, offers cash on delivery and 7-day returns, which means you can inspect the piece in hand and still change your mind. Whatever store you use, know the return window and keep the packaging until you are sure.

sections.heading: Red flags that usually mean poor quality
paragraphs: Some warning signs are hard to miss once you know them:
list: A strong chemical or paint smell when you open the box.
Plating that comes off on your fingers or on a white tissue.
Stones that look cloudy, chipped or mismatched straight out of the packet.
Ear hooks that are a different, grey-coloured metal from the rest of the earring.
A dori that is thin and fraying, or attached with a single weak loop.

sections.heading: Match quality to how you will use it
paragraphs: Not every piece needs to be the best you can find. For a single theme party, a lightweight, inexpensive piece is perfectly fine. For something you plan to wear across a whole wedding season, or a set you want to pass on to a sister or daughter, it is worth spending a little more on solid brass, better plating and well-set stones.

If you are just starting to build a collection, a good approach is to buy one versatile, well-made set, such as a [Kundan necklace set](/women/necklaces) in a neutral gold tone, and add smaller pieces from the [under ₹999](/shop?max=999) range around it.

faq.q: How can I tell if imitation jewellery is good quality?
faq.a: Check for even plating on the back, firmly set stones, smooth edges, strong hooks and a necklace that drapes flat. Avoid pieces with glue marks or bare patches.
Not always. Weight often signals a brass base, but comfort and balance matter just as much, especially for earrings.

faq.q: How do I check jewellery quality when buying online?
faq.a: Read the material details, zoom into all photos, look for natural-light and customer images, and confirm the return policy before ordering.

faq.q: Does good imitation jewellery turn black?
faq.a: All plated jewellery can darken with time, but good plating and proper care slow it down considerably.
